book.title: Quantum Mechanics
book.description:
This book proposes a rigorous formalization of modern quantum mechanics. Going beyond the scope of conventional introductory textbooks, it develops the essential tools of mathematical physics, from Hilbert spaces to advanced spectral theory, including topology and geometry.

This treatise is intended for readers who seek, beyond computational practice, to understand the logical necessity and foundation of the structures in use. The text addresses interpretational issues directly, with a detailed analysis of the measurement problem and decoherence, while also presenting alternative theories and their experimental constraints.

Intended for master's students, doctoral students, and researchers, it aims at a comprehensive command of the theory, uniting technical rigor with conceptual depth.

about.label: ABOUT THE BOOK
about.authorBioRest: His research interests include the laws of gravitation, quantum mechanics and its foundations, and symbolic regression as a machine learning task. This book grew from lecture notes developed over many years of teaching at graduate and advanced undergraduate level.
about.aboutProjectLead: This site and the book are under development. Lessons and exercises will be added gradually.
about.aboutProjectOutlineBody: Part I, isolated systems: mathematical formalism (mathematical physics), postulates, basic applications. Part II, interacting systems: entanglement, decoherence, measurement theory. Part III: interpretations of quantum mechanics and alternative theories. Part IV: quantum information, quantum algorithms. Part V: quantum gravity.
about.aboutBookBody2: The text develops quantum mechanics from first principles, assuming a strong background in classical mechanics, electrodynamics, and mathematics. Proofs are given in full whenever they clarify the physics, and many worked examples complement the theoretical exposition.
about.translationWarning: This book is primarily written in French. Translations are produced with AI assistance and may contain errors; the French text is the reference version.

foundational-experiments.title: General Introduction and Foundational Experiments
foundational-experiments.description: Historical experiments that invalidate classical mechanics.

introduction.title: Lesson 1
introduction.subtitle: Stern-Gerlach Experiment
introduction.description: Experimental introduction to spin, magnetic moment, and quantization observed in the Stern-Gerlach experiment.

interference.title: Lesson 2
interference.subtitle: Interference, Paths, and Quantum Eraser
interference.description: Mach-Zehnder interferometer, superposition vs. mixture, path marking, quantum eraser, and complementarity.

hilbert-spaces.title: Hilbert Spaces and Dirac Notation
hilbert-spaces.description: Hilbert space structure, topological dual, and Dirac notation in finite and infinite dimension.

espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-1.title: Lesson 1
espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-1.subtitle: Hilbert Spaces
espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-1.description: Vector spaces, norms, inner products, strong topology, completeness, and Hilbert bases to establish quantum mechanics' formal framework.

espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-2.title: Lesson 2
espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-2.subtitle: Dual Space, Kets, Bras, Adjoint
espaces-de-hilbert-lecon-2.description: Construction of the topological dual, identification via the Riesz representation theorem, and physical interpretation.

espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-1.title: Sheet 1
espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-1.subtitle: Dirac Notation — Finite Dimension
espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-1.description: Algebraic rules of quantum calculation valid in any dimension, then the matrix reference sheet in finite dimension.

espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-2.title: Sheet 2
espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-2.subtitle: Dirac Notation — Infinite Dimension
espaces-de-hilbert-fiche-2.description: Hilbert representation of point-particle quantum mechanics, position and momentum operators, and Dirac delta.

linear-operator-theory.title: Linear Operator Theory
linear-operator-theory.description: Topology of Hilbert spaces, bounded and unbounded linear operators, and spectral theory.

operateurs-lineaires-lecon-1.title: Lesson 1
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-1.subtitle: Topology of Hilbert Spaces
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-1.description: Strong/weak convergences, Cauchy sequences, completeness, and topological structures of Hilbert spaces.

operateurs-lineaires-lecon-2.title: Lesson 2
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-2.subtitle: Linear Operator Theory
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-2.description: Definition, domain, composition, continuity, and norm of linear operators in Hilbert space.

operateurs-lineaires-lecon-3.title: Lesson 3
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-3.subtitle: Bounded Operators
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-3.description: Algebra of bounded operators, self-adjoint and unitary operators, spectral theorem in finite dimension.

operateurs-lineaires-lecon-4.title: Lesson 4
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-4.subtitle: Unbounded Operators
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-4.description: Densely defined operators, closure, adjoint, self-adjoint extensions, and essential self-adjointness criteria.

operateurs-lineaires-lecon-5.title: Lesson 5
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-5.subtitle: Spectral Theory
operateurs-lineaires-lecon-5.description: Spectrum and resolvent of self-adjoint operators, spectral measure, general spectral theorem, and functional calculus.

operateurs-lineaires-fiche-1.title: Sheet 1
operateurs-lineaires-fiche-1.subtitle: Atlas of Linear Operators
operateurs-lineaires-fiche-1.description: Catalogue of the main linear operators and their spectral properties.

postulates.title: Postulates
postulates.description: Core axioms of the theory, interpretations, and physical consequences of measurement.

postulats-lecon-1.title: Lesson 1
postulats-lecon-1.subtitle: Measurement, Dynamics, and Interpretation
postulats-lecon-1.description: Presentation of quantum postulates, Born rule, wavefunction collapse, and the Schrodinger equation.

applications.title: Applications
applications.description: Computational methods and operator tools to connect postulates with concrete predictions.

applications-lecon-1.title: Lesson 1
applications-lecon-1.subtitle: Potential Barriers
applications-lecon-1.description: Transmission, reflection, tunneling, and energy dependence of states across potential barriers.

applications-lecon-2.title: Lesson 2
applications-lecon-2.subtitle: Harmonic Oscillator
applications-lecon-2.description: Energy level quantization, creation/annihilation operators, and eigenstates of the harmonic oscillator.

applications-lecon-3.title: Lesson 3
applications-lecon-3.subtitle: Spin
applications-lecon-3.description: Pauli matrices, spin measurement, dynamics in magnetic fields, and two-level applications.

applications-lecon-4.title: Lesson 4
applications-lecon-4.subtitle: Quantum Dynamics
applications-lecon-4.description: Unitary evolution, Schrodinger equation, Schrodinger/Heisenberg pictures, and propagators.

interacting-systems.title: Interacting Systems
interacting-systems.description: Composite states, entanglement, couplings, and dynamics of non-isolated quantum systems.

decoherence-and-quantum-measurement.title: Decoherence and Quantum Measurement
decoherence-and-quantum-measurement.description: Classical emergence, the measurement problem, and the role of the environment.
